commits.message:
refactor(facts): the composed usage is the cost and tokens the payload reads, the metrics fold is the base type, and the owners' tests assert their folds (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.yb3)

Review (high) fixes: usageOver answers { cost, tokens } and the one-field wrapper, officialCost and the spread of the fold's other fields go; MetricsFold is declared on its own and MetricsInfo extends it; the pure context overlay no longer logs; the store and metrics tests assert the folds, and usageOver and metricsOver have in-process tests of their own.

refactor(facts): a session's facts carry each transcript fold alone, and the payload lays the hook over it (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.yb3)

Gather will know a session by its locator alone, so no fact may mix the
request's hook into a transcript fold. Three did: usage (the hook's cost over
the priced fold), context (the hook's native window over the fold's tokens)
and metrics (the hook's durations and lines over the fold's counts).

The usage store, the context provider and the metrics provider now refresh and
answer their folds alone, keyed by the session and read from its transcript.
The overlays are pure functions beside their contract types (`usageOver`,
`contextOver`, `metricsOver`), applied where the payload is composed, which
already holds the hook. The document types those three facts as the folds, so
the compiler refuses a hook value in it. The stored usage record loses its
`cost`/`officialCost` copies.

The context fold is now read for every session, where before it was read only
when the hook carried no native window: the document is total and cannot know
which hook it will be composed with.

The bar is unchanged. `check`'s fixture and the session rig carry their cost,
durations and window in their hooks, as Claude Code sends them, so the
payload goldens gain the raw `cost` and `context_window` blocks and nothing
else.

test(daemon): a test closes every home it opens, so no file's periods tick inside a later file's close case (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.88o) (#708)

* test(daemon): a test closes every home it opens, so no file's periods tick inside a later file's close case (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.88o)

The daemon close case's leftover timers were never its daemon's. The
payload-owners helpers held a real host source through a home nobody
closed, and the git cache tests left their providers open, so their
periods re-armed for the life of the Jest worker. Held together, they
re-arm together, so the close case failed only when that turn fell inside
it. An audit of armed periods at each file's end now reads zero in every
worker-tier file.

* test(daemon): a home closes through the case's cleanups, and each test's one close path is its afterEach (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.88o)

declaredLanes takes the cleanups array the other rig helpers take, so a
caller cannot open a home without handing over its close. The git cache
cases drop the trailing closes their afterEach now repeats; the closes a
case asserts across, or orders before a repo's removal, stay.

* test(daemon): a lane declaration that throws fails the payload helper with its stack (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.88o)

The helper dropped declareLanes' faults, so a broken owner fixture read as
an unexplained failed cell; it closes the home and throws them instead, as
the daemon logs them as errors. requestPayload's header says its home lives
for one request.
